The New York Times 1981 report (https://www.nytimes.com/1981/05/20/us/conservatives-gather-in-umbrella-council-for-a-national-policy.html) supports that more than 50 conservatives convened a new Council for National Policy and describes its early aims and leadership. It does not connect Donald Trump to the organization or meeting.

Documented’s report (https://documented.org/investigations/documented-has-obtained-a-recent-council-for-national-policy-membership-list) discusses separately published CNP directories; the accessible material does not establish Trump’s membership, role, or an action involving him. Recasting this as CNP founding history would describe an unrelated organizational event rather than resolve the Trump-specific record.

Hold pending a readable, reliable membership record naming Trump or credible event-specific reporting documenting his participation or a CNP action involving him. A list compiler’s incomplete-list description alone cannot establish Trump’s membership or role.

The coordinator and prior proposal leave the shooting entry held because the supplied attack reporting did not itself establish a Trump connection. The official government transcript independently verifies Trump’s direct response on August 5, 2019, so the record can be narrowed to that statement.
The casualty figures in this proposal are explicitly attributed to Trump’s remarks. No independent count or claim about the shooter’s motive is added.
The proposal treats the remarks as a distinct statement event and must remain separate from records describing the August 4 shooting itself.

proposal.title: Trump Addresses the Dayton Shooting in August 5 Remarks
proposal.description_short: On August 5, 2019, Trump addressed the Dayton shooting in White House remarks on the attacks in Ohio and Texas.
proposal.description_medium: On August 5, 2019, Trump delivered White House remarks about the Dayton and El Paso attacks. He said the Dayton shooting killed nine people and injured 27, expressed sympathy for victims and survivors, said he had spoken with Ohio Governor Mike DeWine and Dayton Mayor Nan Whaley, and directed federal authorities to provide needed assistance.
proposal.description_long: President Donald Trump delivered remarks on August 5, 2019, in the White House Diplomatic Reception Room about the weekend attacks in Dayton, Ohio, and El Paso, Texas. The official transcript records that he described the Dayton gunman as having killed nine people and injured 27. Trump expressed sympathy for victims, families, and survivors. He said he had spoken with Ohio Governor Mike DeWine and Dayton Mayor Nan Whaley to express support, and that he was in close contact with Attorney General William Barr and FBI Director Christopher Wray. He also said he had directed federal authorities to provide whatever assistance was needed. This proposal describes Trump’s public response as a separate dated statement event; it does not treat him as responsible for the shooting or claim anything about the gunman’s motive. The transcript is the basis for the date, setting, casualty figures as Trump stated them, named contacts, and assistance directive. Keep this separate from any entry about the August 4 attack itself, and deduplicate statement records by the August 5 transcript rather than conflating them with reporting on the attack.

supports: The remarks were delivered by President Donald Trump on August 5, 2019, in the White House Diplomatic Reception Room, and addressed attacks in Dayton and El Paso.
Trump stated that the Dayton attack killed nine people and injured 27, expressed sympathy for victims and survivors, and said he had spoken with Ohio Governor Mike DeWine and Dayton Mayor Nan Whaley.
Trump said he was in close contact with Attorney General William Barr and FBI Director Christopher Wray and had directed federal authorities to provide needed assistance.

proposal.duplicate_event_guard: Deduplicate by the August 5, 2019 statement and official transcript URL. Keep separate from any August 4 Dayton shooting event; do not describe Trump as the shooter or infer the perpetrator’s motive.

The official U.S. Sentencing Commission chair’s January 24 remarks say Judges Claria Horn Boom and John Gleeson’s service ended earlier that month, but do not say President Trump removed them; this documents two departures, not the alleged three firings on January 20 (https://www.ussc.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/amendment-process/public-hearings-and-meetings/20250124/remarks.pdf).

The Commission’s January 24 release gives its membership at that meeting but supplies no notice that Trump removed three commissioners (https://www.ussc.gov/about/news/press-releases/january-24-2025). The official record does not establish who the alleged three people were, whether they were fired, or the date and reason.

28 U.S.C. § 991(a) does state that Commission members may be removed only for neglect of duty, malfeasance, or other good cause, but the statute does not prove a removal or litigation over one (https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=%28title%3A28+section%3A991+edition%3Aprelim%29+OR+%28granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title28-section991%29&f=treesort&num=0&edition=prelim).

Hold until a primary termination/removal communication or reliable contemporaneous report identifies the affected commissioners and establishes an actual Trump removal; any claimed legal dispute also needs its case filing or docket and procedural status. Do not transfer facts from removals involving another commission.
